items.content_excerpt: $AMD — More investigation headlines. But how much new evidence? Rosen Law Firm announced an investigation into potential securities claims on Nov. 22, adding another legal headline to AMD’s China-related controversy. My view: investors should separate the number of announcements from the amount of new information. A law firm announcing an investigation is not a regulatory finding—and several announcements can still revolve around the same underlying allegations. That doesn’t make the underlying questions disappear. I want specifics: what transactions occurred, what permissions applied, and whether AMD’s disclosures accurately described the exposure. I remain cautious about the uncertainty. But I won’t count repeated headlines as independent proof. New documents or a substantive company response would carry more weight with me. Bears: which specific piece of evidence most strongly supports your case? Bulls: what disclosure would make you stop dismissing this as noise?

items.title: $SLS $CAPR $SVRA $XBI Good morning, SELLAS community! I believe the relatively modest p-value of 0.035 in REGAL is largely related to the sm
items.content_excerpt: $SLS $CAPR $SVRA $XBI Good morning, SELLAS community! I believe the relatively modest p-value of 0.035 in REGAL is largely related to the small trial size and the limited number of death events. Let's compare GPS with Onureg: Onureg (QUAZAR): 472 patients, HR 0.69, p = 0.0009, median OS 24.7 vs. 14.8 months. GPS (REGAL): 126 patients, HR 0.59, p = 0.035, median OS 24.0 vs. 14.7 months. GPS achieved a numerically stronger hazard ratio despite being studied in a more challenging CR2+ population. In my view, if REGAL had enrolled 400 patients and maintained the same treatment effect and event proportion, the p-value could have been significantly lower, potentially below 0.01. Of course, these are different trials and populations, so this is not a head-to-head comparison. I'm looking forward to seeing the full Kaplan-Meier curves. Just my personal analysis, not financial advice.

Dell and HPE both report before Thanksgiving, and PCE inflation hits Wednesday morning right before the holiday. A lot packed into a short week. WHERE WE STAND • The S&P 500 and the Dow are officially in correction, both more than 10% off their highs. The Nasdaq wiped out its whole gain for 2026 and just had its worst week since March 2020 • $NVDA beat, guided to $130B for next quarter (above estimates), and still had its worst week since 2008. Friday's 14% drop came after a report that the SEC is looking at its accounting. A probe doesn't mean they did anything wrong, but with no permanent CEO in place, the timing couldn't be worse • VIX closed near 36. Fear is high and I don't see sellers backing off yet If Nvidia can beat and raise and still get crushed, nobody should be counting on earnings to turn this around. Keep that in mind this week. HPE (MONDAY AFTER THE CLOSE) • They guided to $13.9B to $14.8B in revenue and $1.20 to $1.30 in adjusted EPS • Record $6.8B AI systems backlog last quarter, plus Oracle is putting HPE's Juniper networking gear into a huge AI buildout • $HPE was already sliding hard before Friday, and options are pricing in a double-digit move • Networking is the best part of their story, but it still depends on the AI buildout continuing. If the money funding it dries up, one good quarter won't change much DELL (TUESDAY AFTER THE CLOSE) • $95B AI server backlog, with $49B in revenue guided for the quarter and about $19B of that from AI servers • My concern is how much of that backlog actually turns into cash. A big chunk comes from neoclouds, the most debt-heavy, hardest-hit group in this whole selloff • Memory prices keep going up and Dell has to eat it unless they can pass it on. That's a margin problem • $DELL is already down roughly half from its September high. Cheap doesn't mean safe if the backlog starts slipping Then Wednesday morning we get PCE. Almost every Fed official at the October meeting expected more hikes, and futures already have one fully priced for December. A hot number makes things worse for anything running on debt, and the AI buildout runs on a lot of it. WHAT I'M DOING • Not holding anything into Dell or HPE earnings. Both can gap 10% or more either way, so I'd rather react than guess • If $SPY and $QQQ bounce early in the week (thin holiday trading can do that), I'm using it to lighten up on AI hardware and look for short setups • Listening for anything on order pushouts, customer financing and cash flow. That matters more to me than whether they beat • Trading smaller. With the VIX this high, normal size is too much risk • Mostly cash until I see real signs the selling is done Bullseye Crew, I'll see you in the chat room this week. 🎯
